propositions: Relations exist whose two applications are in the same model and whose scope is not container (i.e. not subordinate).
note: The code has no term 'non-cross-model relation'; scope is container if either endpoint is container-scoped, else global. Naming caveat: subordinate and peer relations are also same-model, so the term is a doc convention narrower than its literal reading.

propositions: Secret labels are free-form strings chosen by the charm, constrained only to be non-empty and unique per owner/consumer.
note: Only checks found: empty label rejected (state.go:2109, 2154) and uniqueness per application/unit owner (state.go:280-360). No format regex for labels.

propositions: A subordinate application is deployed with zero units.
Units of a subordinate appear only when a container-scoped relation to a principal is made.
note: Server rejects units ('subordinate application must be deployed without units'); CLI rejects --num-units/--to and --constraints (cmd/juju/application/deployer/charm.go:134-141).

propositions: Juju distinguishes Kubernetes clouds from all other (machine) cloud types.
note: The only CAAS cloud type is 'kubernetes'; every other type is IAAS/machine. Definition is near-tautological; a sharper one: any cloud whose type is not kubernetes.

propositions: A cloud is an entity with an API.
It provides compute and networking, and optionally storage.
correction: To Juju, a cloud is a backing substrate that supplies compute (and usually networking and storage) for units; most clouds are API-driven, but the manual (unmanaged) cloud is just a set of SSH-reachable machines with no provisioning API, and networking features such as spaces are optional per provider.
note: Unmanaged provider StartInstance returns errNoStartInstance; networking is an optional capability (environs/networking.go:15-18 SupportsNetworking).

propositions: Several CLI commands take a machine argument or flag.
note: Examples: exec --machine, add-unit/deploy --to placement (cmd/juju/application/addunit.go:99), ssh, remove-machine, show-machine, retry-provisioning, debug-log.

propositions: A charm consuming a (user) secret may attach its own consumer label to it.
'vault-api-token' is a valid label.
note: Consumer labels are stored and resolved per unit (GetURIByConsumerLabel); any non-empty string is accepted.

propositions: A cross-model relation joins applications in different models.
It cannot be subordinate (container-scoped).
It may span controllers.
note: Offers reject endpoints with container scope (scope_id 1). Cross-controller supported via offerer_controller_uuid (domain/crossmodelrelation/service/migration.go:92). Different clouds follows from different controllers/models; not separately coded.

propositions: The implicit juju-info endpoint is added to every charm.
It is only useful for machine charms.
It exists to let subordinates attach to a principal lacking a suitable interface.
correction: Juju adds an implicit global-scoped juju-info provider endpoint to every charm that does not declare one; its common use is letting a container-scoped subordinate attach to any principal, but it can also serve ordinary global relations, and the code places no machine-only restriction on it.
note: encodeJujuInfoRelation uses Scope: ScopeGlobal (domain/application/state/metadata.go:468-474); container scope arises when either endpoint is container-scoped (relation.go:286). 'Only useful for machine charms' is a usage judgement; no model-type check found in domain/relation.

propositions: Units granted access to a secret can set their own consumer label.
Peer units get implicit access.
Peer units assign their own consumer label.
correction: Any unit granted access to a secret can assign its own consumer label (e.g. shared-db-creds); peer units of an application-owned secret get implicit access but address it through the owner label, so no separate consumer label is recorded for them.
note: ProcessCharmSecretConsumerLabel: for app-owned secrets the leader and peer units use the owner label and labelToUpdate is set to nil to preserve uniqueness (service.go:745-757). Implicit access is for application-owned secrets only (getAppOwnedOrUnitOwnedSecretMetadata, service.go:794-823).

propositions: Juju assigns each secret a URI.
'6k7n4ps1vj2d9b318x5w' is a valid secret ID.
correction: Juju assigns the secret a URI of the form secret:<xid>, a 20-character base32hex ID whose last character is 0 or g, e.g. secret:9m4e2mr0ui3e8a215n4g.
note: idSnippet = [0-9a-v]{19}[0g]; the example ends in 'w' (outside a-v and not 0/g), so ParseURI rejects it. The canonical form also carries the 'secret:' scheme (SecretScheme, secret.go:58).

propositions: Endpoint role affects firewall rules.
Requirer is treated as client, provider as server.
Ports are opened on the provider side.
correction: Endpoint role affects firewalling only for cross-model relations: Juju treats the requirer as client and applies the requirer's egress CIDRs as ingress rules on the provider side; the ports themselves are opened by the charm, not by Juju.
note: Firewaller consumer side dispatches on role (firewaller.go:1819); offerer side skips when local endpoint is requirer (1926). No role-based port opening for same-model relations.
